newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends lower but bottom in sight.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends lower but bottom in sight.

text.p: NWE gasoline traded lower on Friday as demand remained patchy and supply fairly sloppy, traders said.
"A bit was done in the morning but since then it's being incredibly quiet," said one trader.
Eurograde barges were done earlier in the day in the low $190s -- once at $191.50 and twice at $192 per tonne fob ARA.
Swaps were similarly weak with April quoted at $191/$193, and May at $194/195.50.
Many traders said they felt the market had reached its bottom, and that prices would either plateau or head higher over the coming week.
"Sellers are holding on to material on the expectation that prices will go higher," said one trader.
It was all quiet on the cargo front, with traders saying the arbitrage door was barely ajar out of Rotterdam, while movements out of places such as Milford Haven looked like a slightly better bet.
Traders noted that cargoes would have to be at least 60,000 tonnes in size to make shipping across the Atlantic worthwhile.
